samples.summary: Structural undo at the tail of an axis is not treated as structural, so the task's criterion 4 (undoing a row/column insert or delete selects those rows/columns as a HEADER selection) is unmet for the last row/column. diffAxisSpan returns undefined for any diff confined to the tail, so undoing a delete-of-the-last-row, or an insert appended past the used range, falls through to the cell branch and yields selectionType 'cell'. The checklist marks criterion 4 done and records this only under 'Known limitations'; the new sheet.md text mentions the tail fall-through but not that it costs the header selection at the edge.
samples.evidence: diffAxisSpan: 'if (head === shorter) return undefined;' // 'identical, or a pure append/truncate at the tail'; sheet.md: 'An axis diff confined to the **tail** is not a structural edit ... so those fall through to the cell branch.'

samples.summary: The resolver derives full-width/full-height ranges for row/column selections that no consumer uses, so the same derivation now exists at three layers. resolveUndoSelection emits {r:from,c:1}..{r:to,c:colOrder.length}; Sheet.applyUndoSelection discards the reported width and rebuilds it from this.dimension.columns; Spreadsheet.focusUndoSelection discards the range shape entirely and calls selectRow/selectRowRange with the indices only. The new workbook/undo-selection.test.ts asserts those unused widths (e.g. expecting [{r:2,c:1},{r:2,c:3}]), locking in values that never reach the view. A single canonical shape (indices in the selection; width filled by the engine that knows the dimension) would avoid the divergence.
samples.evidence: undo-selection.ts row branch: 'c: Math.max(1, snapshotAfter.colOrder.length)'; sheet.ts applyUndoSelection: '{ r: end.r, c: this.dimension.columns }'; spreadsheet.ts focusUndoSelection: 'this.sheet.selectRow(start.r)'

samples.summary: Applying an UndoSelection is implemented twice with different mechanics: Sheet.applyUndoSelection assigns activeCell/ranges directly and re-establishes the merge invariant via normalizeRefToAnchor / expandRangeToMergedBoundaries, while Spreadsheet.focusUndoSelection (the cross-tab path) re-derives the same selection through selectStart/selectEnd/selectRow/selectColumn. The two will answer the same question differently as either evolves (e.g. the merge-normalisation fix that was added to applyUndoSelection has no counterpart in focusUndoSelection, which relies on selectStart's behaviour instead). Reusing one entry point on Sheet for both the same-tab and post-tab-switch case would keep one answer.
samples.evidence: sheet.ts applyUndoSelection sets fields + merge normalisation; spreadsheet.ts focusUndoSelection re-implements via selection commands

samples.summary: Yorkie-document-shape knowledge is placed in the engine package, against the boundary docs/design/sheets/collaboration.md states it mitigates for. The resolver hard-codes the CRDT JSONPath layout of the *frontend's* Yorkie document ('$.sheets.' prefix, rowOrder/colOrder/rangeStyles/colWidths field names, operation path/key semantics), while collaboration.md's mitigation is 'keeping generic worksheet helpers in the shared package and Yorkie-specific axis/structure orchestration in local frontend helpers'. The UndoOperation type is structurally typed to avoid the SDK import, but the path grammar it parses is still the collaboration layer's, not the engine's. No behavioural consequence; only the layer is off.
samples.evidence: const SheetPathPrefix = '$.sheets.'; parseSheetPath/collectTouches switch on 'rowOrder' | 'colOrder' | 'rangeStyles' | 'colWidths' ...; collaboration.md 'Store boundary leakage' mitigation

samples.summary: Range-carrying edits other than rangeStyles get no selection, so the criterion 'a range edit (paste, style, sort, fill) selects the whole range' is only partly met. conditionalFormats and dataValidations hold their ranges inside array element values, which the operations do not carry and which snapshotTabs does not snapshot, so undoing such an edit falls to the final 'tab but no range' branch and leaves the cursor where it is -- the original symptom, for that class of edit. The same before/after diff used for rangeStyles would cover it; the task records this as a known limitation but the new design-doc section only excuses coordinate-free steps (freeze pane, filter).
searchedFor: grep conditionalFormats in packages/sheets/src and frontend yorkie-store
samples.evidence: UndoTabSnapshot = { rowOrder, colOrder, rangeStyles }; default branch comment: 'Freeze pane, filter state, hidden rows, charts, comments: the tab is known but the change has no coordinates.'

samples.summary: Two undo/redo invocation paths remain and now diverge in what they refresh: the keyboard shortcut in worksheet.ts calls updateFreezeState() + render() + scrollIntoView(), while Spreadsheet.undo()/redo() (the toolbar/public path, which this diff touched to add revealActiveCell) render, reveal and notify but never updateFreezeState. Since the point of this change was to make the public path match the keyboard path, the remaining asymmetry is worth folding into one method.
